annotation.title_clean: AI Foundation Models: Technical update report
annotation.title_en: AI Foundation Models: Technical update report
named_instruments_referenced: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Bill
annotation.summary_en: The UK Competition and Markets Authority's April 2024 update on AI foundation models describes developments in the market and the main inputs: data, compute, chips, expertise and funding. It reports stakeholder feedback and confirms the CMA's competition and consumer-protection principles. It names three key risks to fair, open and effective competition and sets out next steps, including enforcement under new powers.
key_provisions_or_claims: Confirms the CMA's AI principles: access, diversity, choice, fair dealing, transparency and accountability
Names three key risks to competition: incumbents controlling key inputs, incumbents' market power in deployment, and partnerships that entrench positions
Warns of possible 'winner-takes-all' dynamics in foundation-model markets
Expects new powers under the DMCC Bill to enforce consumer law directly, with penalties of up to 10% of worldwide turnover
Plans a paper on AI accelerator chips, joint work with the Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum (DRCF) and a joint statement with the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO)
